english: 25 Chronography of Bar Ebraya (Barhebraeus).
And he asked leave of the king,
that they should not trouble him.
But when the Greeks heard that Diogenes had been captured,
they proclaimed Michael son of Constantine as their king.
And this man seized his mother,
who was the wife of Diogenes,
and shut her up in a monastery at Baqtira.
And Caesarius, Ioani, was her uncle.
But when Diogenes came to the land of the Romans,
and heard what had happened,
he went up to his fortress of Dukia.
And he found in it two hundred thousand denarii,
and sent them to the Sultan with two emirs who had gone with him,
and informed the Sultan.
And he put on the monastic habit,
and dwelt in his fortress.
And he sent to Michael and said:
"Until now I have contended in a good contest for the sake of the Christians' safety, and see.
You, however, blessed be your kingdom,
and good is the work of one who made you king,
because you had no right to it.
But I counsel you in faith not to break the peace that I made with the Sultan,
otherwise no rest remains, neither for you
nor for the Christians."
And Michael accepted his kindness and said:
"I will not go out from your counsel."
But after some days men plotted against him,
and he sent to Diogenes and said to him:
"If you are truly a monk,
why do you have a seat in a fortress? It is proper that you go down to one of the monasteries,
and we shall send guardians to it in the fortress."
But Diogenes was angered and said:
"Out of the whole kingdom of the Romans not even one fortress is left to me."
And he arose and sent baggage vessels,
and took the caravans of the merchants of Dukia as if in the manner of a raid,
and gathered an army for himself.
And when the son of Sennacherib, the patriarch of Little Armenia, came to him,
he seized him and blinded his eyes,
and took from him eighty kentenaria of gold.
And he grew strong, and came to Melitene,
and sent to the Sultan Alp Arslan
and sought help from him.
And the Sultan promised him
that he would go in person to help him wherever need called.
And after these things,
Diogenes departed from Melitene to Cilician Gaul.
And Ioani came against him,
and subdued him in the city of Adana.
And when he had seized him,
he sent and informed King Michael.
